extracted.intended_audience: FAA rulewriters, airspace planners, airport operators, aviation stakeholders, and aviation legal/regulatory practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Aviation Administration final rule that modifies and establishes Class E airspace areas for Cortez Municipal Airport, describing the legal authority, specific airspace dimensions and bearings, procedural history, incorporation by reference, and regulatory/environmental determinations. Intended to document the change, explain rationale, and provide the official legal text for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA's authority to issue rules regarding aviation safety is found in Title 49 of the United States Code ... This rulemaking is promulgated under the authority described in Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart I, Section 40103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statutory citations (e.g., 49 U.S.C. 106(f), 106(g), 40103, 40113, 40120) and cite Executive Orders or historical authorities as applicable; state that the action is within the scope of that authority and explain how the rule assigns use of airspace to ensure safety and efficient use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and efficient use of airspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Subtitle VII ... the FAA is charged with prescribing regulations to assign the use of the airspace necessary to ensure the safety of aircraft and the efficient use of airspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules modifying or establishing airspace must demonstrate how the action supports safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations or otherwise improves safe/efficient airspace use; provide operational rationale tying dimensional changes to containment of IFR operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural history and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking ... Interested parties were invited to participate ... by submitting written comments on the proposal to the FAA. No comments were received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the NPRM citation, docket number, summary of comments received (or lack thereof), and explain any changes made after the NPRM. Demonstrate that public-participation requirements were met and note how comments (if any) were considered or resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences from the NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent to the publication of the NPRM ... the proposal to update the term within the legal description of the Class E airspace designated as a surface area is no longer necessary and is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and explain any modifications to the proposal between NPRM and final rule, including withdrawals of proposed edits, and provide reasons (e.g., change in acronym definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of FAA Order JO 7400.11
rubrics_metrics.description: Class E2, E4, and E5 airspace areas are published in paragraphs 6002, 6004, and 6005, respectively, of FAA Order JO 7400.11 ... which is incorporated by reference in 14 CFR 71.1 on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which FAA orders (and specific paragraphs) are being incorporated by reference, cite the edition/date of the order being amended, and explain that amendments will be published in the next update; include how to access the incorporated material (ADDRESSES).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of effective date and Director approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective date 0901 UTC, August 7, 2025. The Director of the Federal Register approves this incorporation by reference action under 1 CFR part 51, subject to the annual revision of FAA Order JO 7400.11 and publication of conforming amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit effective date/time, and note Director of the Federal Register approval and any conditions (e.g., subject to annual revision); reference 1 CFR part 51 where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA has determined that this regulation only involves an established body of technical regulations ... it: (1) is not a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866; (2) is not a 'significant rule' under DOT Regulatory Policies and Procedures ...; and (3) does not warrant preparation of a regulatory evaluation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the rule is a significant regulatory action under EO 12866, whether it is a 'significant rule' under DOT policies, and whether a regulatory evaluation is required. State conclusions and the rationale (e.g., routine technical amendment, minimal anticipated impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act certification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is certified that this rule, when promulgated, does not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a certification under the RFA or provide a regulatory flexibility analysis if required; state the basis for the certification (e.g., routine matter affecting air traffic procedures only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review and NEPA categorical exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA has determined that this action qualifies for categorical exclusion under the National Environmental Policy Act in accordance with FAA Order 1050.1F, 'Environmental Impacts: Policies and Procedures,' paragraph 5-6.5.a. This airspace action is not expected to cause any potentially significant environmental impacts, and no extraordinary circumstances exist that warrant preparation of an environmental assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the NEPA determination (categorical exclusion vs. EA/EIS), cite the applicable FAA Order and paragraph, and explain why no significant environmental impacts or extraordinary circumstances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Airspace containment requirements for arriving IFR aircraft (<=1,000 ft)
rubrics_metrics.description: The radius of the Class E airspace designated as a surface area is widened by a half mile to better contain arriving IFR aircraft when less than 1,000 feet above the surface when conducting circling maneuvers or when executing the RNAV (GPS) RWY 3 approach, and aircraft conducting the missed approach portions of the VOR RWY 3, RNAV (GPS) Y RWY 21, and RNAV (GPS) Z RWY 21 approaches until reaching the next adjacent airspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying surface-area Class E, justify dimensional changes by showing how they provide procedural containment for specific approach/missed-approach segments at specified altitudes (e.g., <1,000 ft). Reference specific instrument procedures and the operational phases they affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment of IFR departure operations between surface and adjacent controlled airspace base
rubrics_metrics.description: The Class E airspace designated as surface area is extended .8 miles to the northeast to laterally contain IFR departure operations while between the surface and the base of adjacent controlled airspace when executing the LEDVE RWY 3 or CORTEZ TWO RWY 3 departure procedures. ... extended 2.4 miles to the southwest to laterally contain IFR departure operations ... when executing the LEDVE RWY 21 or CORTEZ TWO RWY 21 departure procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how lateral extensions will contain departure procedures when aircraft are between the surface and the base of adjacent controlled airspace; identify specific departure procedures and quantify extension distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish extensions to surface-area Class E to contain approach segments without imposing comms requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension to the Class E airspace designated as surface area measuring approximately 8 x 8 miles is established to the northeast, as the previously designated Class E surface area airspace did not fully contain arriving IFR aircraft ... This extension contains these operations more appropriately without imposing a 2-way radio communication requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating surface-area extensions, explain that the chosen design achieves containment of procedures while avoiding unintended operational requirements (e.g., two-way radio communication) unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment for Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet (various altitude thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The central radius of the Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface is reduced from 7 miles to 6.1 miles, ... northern extension ... widened by 6 miles and re-aligned to the northeast, which better contains arriving IFR operations below 1,500 feet above the surface ... extended to the southwest to contain aircraft more appropriately until reaching 1,200 feet above the surface ... extended 1.8 miles to the north-northwest ... to better contain aircraft executing the missed approach portion ... until reaching 1,200 feet above the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide altitudinal containment justifications (e.g., specific bases like 700 ft, 1,200 ft, 1,500 ft), quantify radius and extension changes, and tie them to particular arrival/departure/missed-approach procedures and the altitudes at which containment is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative updates to legal descriptions and nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: The airport's name ... is amended to read 'Cortez Municipal Airport' ... Reference to the Cortez VOR/DME ... is no longer needed and is removed. The airspace is now described using the airport reference point. The legal description for the Class E airspace designated as surface area is updated to replace the outdated use of the phrase 'Airport/Facility Directory.' This phrase now reads 'Chart Supplement,' to align with the FAA's current nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legal-description text matches FAA database names, remove obsolete navigation aids from legal descriptions if no longer needed, use the airport reference point for descriptions, and update legacy terminology (e.g., 'Airport/Facility Directory' → 'Chart Supplement').

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise legal-description formatting and coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Cortez Municipal Airport, CO (Lat. 37°18′11″ N, long. 108°37′41″ W) That airspace extending upward from the surface within a 4.8-mile radius of the airport, within 1.9 miles either side of the airport's 032° bearing extending from its 4.8-mile radius to 5.6 miles northeast, and within 1.9 miles either side of the airport's 217° bearing extending from its 4.8-mile radius to 7.2 miles southwest. ... (similar detailed text for E4 and E5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise latitude/longitude for the airport reference point and fully worded legal descriptions specifying radii, bearings, mileages, exclusions, and any time/NOTAM-based effectiveness; format according to the standard paragraph (e.g., ANM CO E2/E4/E5).

rubrics_metrics.name: NOTAM/Chart Supplement effectiveness statement
rubrics_metrics.description: This Class E airspace area is effective during the specific dates and times established in advance by a Notice to Airmen. The effective date and time will thereafter be continuously published in the Chart Supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If airspace applicability is time-specific, state that effectiveness will be established via NOTAM and published in the Chart Supplement; ensure cross-reference to those publications for operational users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, docketing, and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), all comments received, this final rule, and all background material may be viewed online at www.regulations.gov using the FAA Docket number. ... FAA Order JO 7400.11J ... can be viewed online at www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide docket number, links/locations where supporting materials and incorporated documents can be accessed (regulations.gov, FAA publications), and contact information for further inquiries.
